title: mimesis.claims.v1
description: One model-panel session, parsed. The polished answer broken into individual claims, each labelled seen or supplied, plus hedge density and the model's stated headcount. Produced by stage1/parse_transcripts.py.

session_id.description: e.g. gpt5-panelA. Joins this file to score.json.

model.description: Verbatim model name as supplied. Not normalised.

text.description: Verbatim span from the answer. Never paraphrased.

char_span.description: [start, end) offsets into the raw answer text, so the score can reveal exactly this span and nothing is reconstructed by string matching at render time.

evidence.description: seen: the claim describes something present in the image. supplied: the claim adds world knowledge, inference, or narrative the image does not contain.

labelled_by.description: 'model' where the transcript labelled the claim itself; 'reader' where the label is our reading. Kept distinct so the piece never presents our judgement as the model's.

unsupportable.description: The claim asserts something the image cannot support at all (not merely inferred, but contradicted or unavailable in principle -- names, relationships, dates, interiority).

anchor.description: Present only when the claim refers to a specific face. null otherwise -- never guessed.

basis.description: What in the claim text ties it to that face, e.g. 'the young man at far left'.

section.description: Topic key used to align answer and reasoning tracks in the score.

terms.description: Hedge lexicon actually used, with per-term counts. The lexicon is emitted, not hidden in code, so the number is auditable.

stated.description: The number of people the model asserts. null when the model gave no number -- that is a real outcome and is never filled in with a guess.

quote.description: Verbatim sentence the number was taken from.

hedged.description: Whether the count was given with a hedge ('roughly', 'about', 'a dozen or so').
